chunks: In the Name of Allah, the All-beneficent, the All-merciful.

The fortunate Imam-Shaykh and jurist, Abu Ja'far Muhammad ibn Ali ibn al-Husayn ibn Musa ibn Babawayh al-Qummi, the author of this book—may Allah sanctify his soul—said: To proceed: when divine decree drove me to the lands of estrangement, and destiny brought me from there to the land of Balkh, in the district of Ilaq, there arrived there al-Sharif al-Din Abu Abd Allah, known as Ni'mah—and he was Muhammad ibn al-Hasan ibn Ishaq ibn [al-Hasan ibn] al-Husayn ibn Ishaq ibn Musa ibn Ja'far ibn Muhammad ibn Ali ibn al-Husayn ibn Ali ibn Abi Talib, peace be upon them.

Through sitting with him, my joy endured; through remembering him, my breast expanded; and through his affection, my honor was magnified, because of qualities he had gathered alongside his nobility: concealment, righteousness, tranquility, dignity, religiosity, chastity, taqwa, and humility.

He mentioned to me a book composed by Muhammad ibn Zakariyya, the physician al-Razi, which he had entitled 'Man La Yahduruhu al-Tabib,' and he said that it was sufficient in its subject. He asked me to compile for him a book in fiqh, halal and haram, laws and rulings, encompassing all that I had authored on that subject, and that I entitle it 'Kitab Man La Yahduruhu al-Faqih,' so that it would be his point of reference, his basis of reliance, and his means of taking, and so that whoever looks into it, copies it, and acts upon what it contains would share in its reward. This was along with his having copied most of my compilations that accompanied me, having heard them from me, narrated them from me, and become acquainted with their entirety, and they were two hundred and forty-five books.

So I answered him—may Allah perpetuate his success—to that request, because I found him worthy of it. I compiled for him this book by omitting the asanid so that its routes would not become too many, even if its benefits are many. I did not intend in it the intention of the compilers in citing everything they narrated; rather, I intended to cite what I give fatwa by, judge to be sound, and believe to be a proof between me and my Lord—sanctified is His remembrance and exalted is His power.

Everything in it has been extracted from well-known books upon which reliance is placed and to which recourse is made, such as the book of Hariz ibn Abd Allah al-Sijistani, the book of Ubayd Allah ibn Ali al-Halabi, the books of Ali ibn Mahziyar al-Ahwazi, the books of al-Husayn ibn Sa'id, the Nawadir of Ahmad ibn Muhammad ibn Isa, the book Nawadir al-Hikmah compiled by Muhammad ibn Ahmad ibn Yahya ibn Imran al-Ash'ari, the book al-Rahmah of Sa'd ibn Abd Allah, the Jami' of our Shaykh Muhammad ibn al-Hasan ibn al-Walid, may Allah be pleased with him, the Nawadir of Muhammad ibn Abi Umayr, the books of al-Mahasin by Ahmad ibn Abi Abd Allah al-Barqi, and the epistle of my father—may Allah be pleased with him—besides other usul and compilations whose paths of transmission to me are known in the catalogue of the books that I narrated from my shaykhs and forefathers—may Allah be pleased with them.

I exerted my utmost effort in that, seeking help from Allah, trusting in Him, and seeking forgiveness for shortcomings. My success is only through Allah; upon Him I have relied, and to Him I turn in repentance, and He is sufficient for me, and the best trustee.

key_terms.الأَسانِيدِ: chains of transmission that the author intentionally omitted in this work
key_terms.الأُصُولِ: foundational source texts from which the work was derived

key_terms.الحَلالِ: what is permissible in the Sacred Law

key_terms.حُجَّةٌ: binding proof before Allah in matters of religion

ai.seo_question: Why did Shaykh al-Saduq write Man La Yahduruhu al-Faqih and what sources did he rely on?
ai.summary: This prelude explains why Shaykh al-Saduq composed Man La Yahduruhu al-Faqih and the method he followed in compiling it. He states that he omitted the chains of narration, included only what he judged reliable and gave fatwa by, and drew the material from recognized primary Shia sources.
